title: SOCRadar describes WeaveLotus, a suspected Vietnam-linked cluster behind RedOps espionage against Southeast Asian governments
date_note: The Hacker News gives only its own publication day, 27 November; the campaign was observed between August and September 2026, per SOCRadar's analysis as relayed.
org: Government and military organisations in Thailand and the Philippines
geo_basis: country: the article names Thailand and the Philippines as intrusion targets; no city is given
summary: The Hacker News relays SOCRadar's analysis of a previously undocumented cluster it codenamed WeaveLotus. The campaign, RedOps, was observed between August and September 2026, compromising targets in Thailand and the Philippines across five confirmed intrusions. SOCRadar bases the Vietnam link on native Vietnamese-language code comments, without conclusively establishing state sponsorship. In one case 349,782 records were pulled from a downstream application.
plain: Security firm SOCRadar reports a previously undocumented group, WeaveLotus, that broke into Thai and Philippine targets in five confirmed intrusions. It suspects a Vietnam link but has not conclusively shown state sponsorship.
exec: SOCRadar's analysis, as relayed by The Hacker News, describes five confirmed intrusions in Thailand and the Philippines; in one case 349,782 records were pulled from a downstream application.

evidence.quote: The sustained campaign, codenamed RedOps, was observed between August and September 2026.
used to pull 349,782 records from a downstream application

validation.note: Only The Hacker News read; SOCRadar's own report was not found or read.
